root_cause.text: The SMP responder did not enforce the MITM protection bit (SMP_AUTH_MITM) in the pairing response's `auth_req` field when the local security policy required HIGH security (MITM), even though the IO capabilities supported MITM, causing a mismatch that allowed `tk_request()` to select a non-MITM method (JUST_CFM) despite the local requirement.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `auth |= SMP_AUTH_MITM` and `rsp.auth_req |= SMP_AUTH_MITM` after verifying MITM can be achieved, directly addressing the CVE description: "If the initiator omits SMP_AUTH_MITM, the response can also omit it even though the local side still requires MITM. tk_request() then sees an auth value without SMP_AUTH_MITM and may select JUST_CFM."

This allows `tk_request()` (line 610) to select a non-MITM method despite the local requirement, matching the root cause. The fix would need to incorporate local security policy into `auth` before calling `build_pairing_cmd` and `tk_request`.
